descriptive_label_from_index: An arithmetized constructive fundamental theorem of algebra, with a Lean formalization blueprint and exact rational reference programs.

Radical formulae for polynomials through degree four, and the Abel–Ruffini theorem for the generic quintic, with an iPRA arithmetization plan. Its Lean file is a blueprint whose `opaque` declarations are not yet defined.

Lagrange inversion coefficientwise in truncated power series: the Lagrange–Bürmann formulas, Bell-polynomial and Good's multivariate forms, Puiseux-type inversion, explicit inverse radii, Lambert W and Catalan expansions. Its Lean file is a blueprint, not a kernel-checked proof.
Puiseux expansions for exactly presented algebraic coefficients, with explicit convergence radii and tail bounds. It bundles the FTA packet as a dependency.
The impossibility of doubling the cube, trisecting 60° and squaring the circle by straightedge and compass. It is stated as a proof architecture.
The Basel identity, ∑ 1/j² = π²/6, as a universally quantified PRA inequality. Its Lean files are uncompiled specifications and an outline.
A finitary constructive Bohr–Mollerup theorem, with a structured Lean scaffold and roadmap.
Effective versions of both parts of the fundamental theorem of calculus and the finite-order Euler–Maclaurin formula.
Quantitative constructive versions of Cauchy's integral theorem and the residue theorem, stated as schemas.

The Gamma function built from finite Euler products, with explicit error bounds: the Euler integral, functional, reflection, multiplication and beta identities, Bohr–Mollerup, Stirling and Binet formulas. It says its Lean file compiles but leaves the analytic contracts uninstantiated.
Stirling's formula, with finite rational estimates and an induction audit.
Taylor's theorem with integral and Peano remainders, and Cauchy's integral formula.

An atlas of trigonometric identities, with principal inverse-function identities, the derivatives of sine and cosine and the dyadic infinite cosine product. Its checker states 227 identities in 27 families verified exactly. Its Lean files are uncompiled, and two of them contain deliberate `axiom` declarations.
Brun's theorem on twin-prime reciprocals, with a primitive-recursive Cauchy modulus.
The Goldbach–Euler theorem, ∑ 1/(p−1) = 1 over perfect powers p, with an explicit convergence modulus. Its Lean outline has explicit `sorry` obligations.
An explicit arithmetic prime number theorem with quantifier-free induction, and the passage to the logarithmic statement.
Logarithmic-integral strengthenings of the prime number theorem: an explicit stretched-exponential bound on π(n) − Li₂(n), and the full asymptotic expansion with explicit remainders.

Prime distribution, which it calls a partial resolution: Dirichlet's theorem with an explicit bound and sharp Brun–Titchmarsh are proved, while Chebotarev, Siegel–Walfisz and Bombieri–Vinogradov get targets and reductions only. Its Lean files are an uncompiled outline.
Divergence of the reciprocal-prime sum in the explicit form ∑_{p ≤ 2^(2·4^k)} 1/p > k.
Riemann's functional equation for ζ in quantitative form, with a formalization plan for its finite arithmetic content.

Constructive zeta theory in 33 result families: Dirichlet convergence, Euler products, the entire regular part and Stieltjes constants, special values, both functional equations and ξ, the Euler–Hasse series, and an explicit lower bound on the modulus of ζ(1+it). Its Lean files are uncompiled candidates.
Quantitative zero distribution of ζ: nonvanishing regions, trivial zeros, the Riemann–von Mangoldt estimate and local counts. It also certifies one critical-line zero near 1/2 + 14.1347i.

Bell numbers: finite identities, the Dobiński and Comtet formulas, generating functions, Hankel determinants, Touchard congruences, an all-n bound, and the de Bruijn and Moser–Wyman asymptotics with explicit remainders. It states that its finite Lean core compiles; the analytic results remain Lean targets.
Apéry's theorem: ζ(3) is irrational, with an explicit primitive-recursive separation from every rational p/q. Its Lean files are uncompiled.

Selected rational Diophantine geometry: bounded-height enumeration, height inequalities for maps of P¹, rational preperiodic points, conic parametrization, and Fermat's square-area theorem by finite descent. It states that its Lean arithmetic core is compiled.
Størmer's theorem, a constructive Davenport–Schmidt theorem, and Roth cutoffs for quadratic irrationals. It says the general effective Roth cutoff is not proved and its Lean files are not compiled.
Logical obstructions to the unrestricted statements, with constructive scalar and simultaneous Dirichlet approximation and quantitative Kronecker theorems.

Faltings' theorem: it says it does not prove the general theorem in iPRA. It analyses the missing height bound and proves special cases, among them the rational points of the Fermat quartic. It states that its three Lean modules compile.
Sharp constructive Hurwitz approximation and quantitative constructive Khinchin approximation.
Minkowski's convex-body theorem.

Constructive Mordell–Weil descent: a general primitive-recursive finite-descent theorem, generators for an elliptic curve relative to a supplied covering list, and an unconditional computation of E(Q) for y² = x³ − u⁴x and products of these. It says it does not give a uniform generator algorithm for arbitrary elliptic curves.
Pell equations for every nonsquare D ≥ 2, with an audit of their algorithms and induction invariants in iPRA.

Siegel's theorem on integral points: it says it does not prove the general theorem in iPRA. It proves a complete constructive Runge case with explicit height bounds and enumeration, the integral points of y² = x²ᵐ + x + 1 and of y² = x⁴ + ax² + b, and the logical link between a uniform iPRA proof and a height bound. It states that its native Lean results compile.
Transcendence of e and π as explicit apartness bounds for nonzero integer polynomials.
Desargues' and Pascal's theorems, with a formalization roadmap and a repository-source audit.
Constructive coordinate proofs of eight theorems: Pappus's harmonic theorem, Ceva, Menelaus, Carnot's conic and polygon theorems, Hoehn, Pappus's hexagon theorem and Brianchon.
Euler's rotation theorem and Rodrigues' formula. It says the unrestricted exact-axis form is not constructively provable (LLPO reduction) and proves constructive replacements.
The sharp planar isoperimetric inequality L² ≥ 4πA, with its equality characterization, for effective presentations.

Constructive isoperimetry, broadening [`isoperimetric_ipra`](geometry/isoperimetric_ipra/) (which it carries under `reused/` and as an appendix): planar and Dido problems, triangle inequalities, a rational Brunn–Minkowski theorem for box unions, the sharp n-dimensional inequality from outer-volume data, finite Sobolev/BV, spherical caps, and the hypercube edge and Harper vertex theorems. Its Lean files are uncompiled outlines.

Mollweide's formulas, the laws of tangents and cotangents with the inradius formula, and the power-of-a-point, tangent-secant, intersecting-chords and intersecting-secants theorems. Its Lean files are not compiled.
Morley's trisector theorem, stated over finite exact certificates.
Pappus's surface and volume centroid theorems, with τ = 2π presented by nested regular polygons.
Exactly five similarity classes of Platonic solids, for constructible-coordinate codes.
Heron's formula and the laws of sines and cosines, in explicit finite arithmetic versions.
Quantitative dimension invariance for finite rational tables, via cubical Sperner parity on staggered grids.
A quantitative Jordan curve theorem for primitive-recursively presented circle embeddings.
